newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen having upward bias, seek 123.50.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen having upward bias, seek 123.50.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures are expected to have an upward bias on Wednesday, due to improved sentiment after the release of weaker-than-expected April machinery orders data on Tuesday.

"JGBs are likely to be solid on the downside. Machinery orders were weak, and there have not been any indicators recently that you could classify as being strong or even mediocre," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
JGBs may be capped on the upside, however, due to about 300 billion to 400 billion yen worth of corporate straight bonds to be launched over this week and next, the trader said.

Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd is expected to launch 40 billion yen worth of straight bonds on Wednesday, and firms such as Nihon Cement Co Ltd and Anritsu Corp may also launch straights within the week, the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Next week, Fujitsu Ltd is expected to launch 100 billion yen worth of straight bonds, and electric power companies are also said to be preparing to launch straights, he said.
Tokyo stocks have been firm amid the yen's rise against the dollar, and the continuation of this trend may stunt rises in JGBs, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
